messages:
Leah: FYI Helionix (new-onboard) sent a surprise burst overnight 24h token delta +180% vs baseline. Putting on our QBR radar and cost ops playbook. :eyes:
Marco: Oof. Any idea which product path? Ingest, embed, or gen?
Dana: Quick look  it's mainly embeddings from the webhook pipeline. 10k small documents getting reprocessed repeatedly.
Omar: I traced client behavior  see repeated 429 retries without exponential backoff. They're re-enqueueing entire batches on error.
Leah: cs-monitor-bot delivered the automated alert earlier:
cs-monitor-bot: ALERT: acct=helionix, metric=tokens_24h, change=+180%, link=https://app.redwood/alerts/hx-4521
Marco: Can we get a 30d risk projection if this pattern continues? Need numbers for the upcoming QBR and renewal playbook.
Dana: Running a quick aggregate now. SQL I used:
```
SELECT account_id, SUM(tokens) as t24h FROM usage WHERE account_id='helionix' AND ts > now()-24h GROUP BY account_id;
```
Results: 3.6M tokens in 24h.
Omar: I've put a temporary 48h throttle on their /v1/embeddings route (soft limit = 2M/day) and tuned the alert to notify the CS owner immediately if it spikes again.
Leah: Thanks. Can we also offer a short enablement session to show client-side backoff + incremental batching? That usually drops embed volume by 5-10x.
Marco: Agreed. Also propose a conservative monthly spend forecast to finance and QBR: if sustained = ~108M tokens/month -> est cost $3.2k (current tier). I'll add conservative/high forecasts in the tracker.
Dana: I'm creating a customer ticket (CS-7892) with the CSV export of the last 7 days and the per-route breakdown. Uploading now.
Omar: FYI I staged a rollout to a smaller quantized embed model for non-critical pipelines. That cuts per-token cost by ~40% while we remediate.
Leah: Nice. For the QBR, let's line up: 1) short-term mitigation applied (throttle + cheaper model) 2) enablement session scheduled 3) billing snapshots and spend scenarios 4) decision on small goodwill credit vs paid enablement.
Marco: Who wants to own the enablement? Dana or Leah?
Dana: I can take it tomorrow 11am PT. Will prep a 20m walkthrough + a 2-page checklist: batching, retry UX, cache TTLs, and a small code snippet for safe retries.
Leah: Assigning: billing forecasts & QBR slides (Marco), enablement + docs (Dana), throttle & model fallback (Omar), post-call notes + renewal tracker update (Leah).
cs-monitor-bot: NOTE: throttle applied to /v1/embeddings for helionix, soft_limit=2000000 tokens/day. Ticket CS-7892 created.
Marco: Posted 7d vs 30d burn scenarios to the tracker. Conservative = $3.2k/mo, aggressive (if spike repeats) = $9k/mo. Adding a renewal risk tag: "usage surge".
Dana: After the call I'll capture any product asks (e.g., built-in client batching helper, server-side idempotency tokens) and mark as P1/P2 for product.
Omar: I'll monitor for 24h and remove the throttle once retries are fixed and usage stabilizes.
Leah: If the customer is amenable we can offer a small one-time credit to offset the unexpected spike and schedule a paid enablement afterwards. Let's table the final ask until after the enablement call.
Marco: Sounds good. Marking as "monitoring; moderate risk" in the renewal workbook. Will push the QBR agenda with these mitigation items.
Leah: Closing loop here  we'll reconvene after the enablement and update renewal playbook entry. :white_check_mark:
